title: Keyshape mapper: hit-curve forecasting, surge-protector TTL autotune, and safe rollback protocol
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: deliver an automated recommendation and safe-apply workflow that proposes optimal cache keys, per-prefix TTL profiles, and batching configuration based on workload-aware hit-curve forecasting. The deliverable is: (1) a Keyshape Mapper service that produces ranking of candidate cache key normalizations and TTL buckets; (2) a Hit-Curve simulator to predict hit-rate / unit-cost tradeoffs under surge scenarios; (3) an orchestration + runbook that safely stages changes, validates impact, and rolls back automatically on guardrail violations.
background: We frequently see downstream cost regressions after naive TTL or keying changes. Existing cache experiments are manual: ad-hoc sampling, static TTLs, and reactive rollbacks. We need an automation layer that understands key lineage, applies conservative key canonicalization, forecasts hit curves (including corner-case surges), and enacts staged policy changes with deterministic rollback triggers.
proposal: Build three components: 1) Keyshape Mapper: analyze request traces to propose candidate canonicalizations (strip affixes, normalize session tokens, collapse user-scoped prefixes) and compute key stability scores; 2) Hit-Curve Simulator: sample historical traces and bootstrap synthetic surge scenarios to estimate hit-rate vs TTL vs batching latency and cost; 3) Safe-Apply Orchestrator: staged rollout (shadow -> 1% -> 10% -> 100%) with automatic rollback rules based on cost deltas, tail-latency regressions, and hit-rate degradation.
modeling_approach: We will use a stratified sampling approach: 14-day sliding window of request traces, grouped by prefix taxonomy, and weighted by traffic variance. Simulator produces 95% CI on hit-rate and cost-per-token under per-prefix TTL sweeps. Key stability score is a composite of prefix entropy, observed mutation rate, and cross-tenant uniqueness. Batching sensitivity is modeled by measured batch-formation latency curves for common sequence length distributions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Keyshape Mapper outputs top-3 canonicalizations per prefix with confidence score and rationale; 2) Simulator forecasts hit-rate and cost delta with <=5% error on historical backtest; 3) Safe-Apply Orchestrator can perform a full staged rollout and auto-rollback in staging cluster; 4) Runbook documented and on-call notified by standard alert channels; 5) Performance metrics surfaced in console: per-prefix hit-rate, cost delta, and rollback events.
rollout_plan: Phase A (staging): run mapper + simulator on last-30 days, validate backtest, run shadow traffic for 48h. Phase B (canary): apply to 1% production traffic for 24h, monitor metrics and cost delta. Phase C (ramped): 10% for 24h, then 50% then 100% if no violations. Automatic rollback triggers: cost increase > 3% absolute or > 20% relative for 30m, P99 latency increase > 50ms sustained for 15m, hit-rate drop > 8% sustained for 30m. Manual abort points at each stage.
metrics_and_dashboards: Track: per-prefix hit-rate, per-prefix QPS, average tokens-per-request, unit-cost per-token, P50/P95/P99 latency, rollout fraction, rollback count. Dashboards: console -> Optimize -> 'Keyshape Recommendations' with drilldowns to request samples and top offending keys.
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for canonicalization rules and stability score, integration test that replays traffic through simulator and validates predicted hit-rate within tolerance, e2e test that runs staged rollout on canary cluster and verifies rollback triggers. Add synthetic surge tests using 'traffic-replay' harness to simulate 3x sustained spike and sudden 10x burst.
runbook_and_ops: Runbook entries: preflight check list, how to interpret mapper confidence, how to abort rollouts manually, post-mortem template. Pager thresholds will match rollback triggers; primary on-call is paged if rollback happens. Post-rollback: automated delta report and required postmortem tagging.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: over-aggressive canonicalization causes key collisions and correctness issues. Mitigation: Keyshape Mapper includes collision detection (hash collisions and user-id mixing) and denies any rule that increases collision score. Risk: simulator underestimates surge profiles. Mitigation: run a battery of synthetic surges (3x, 5x, 10x) and conservative headroom margins.
